advances: The original negative-scalar source has a uniform fourth-moment bound for its height-conditioned transverse total noise at every legal height count and every transverse rank. The new mechanism bounds the original height-zero mass by the adjacent partition-curvature ratio and pairs its suppression with a tilt-sensitive middle-slice variance estimate. It does not equate the two endpoint probabilities outside the three-height case. Thus the averaged total-noise bridge is proved with the original height probabilities, including small height steps and zero-budget top slices.
author: research-agent
proof:
Put \(q=e^\beta\in(0,1)\), \(B_y=L-hy\), and \(p_y=\Pr(Y=y)\) for \(0\le y\le K\). For a nonnegative integer budget \(B\), define
\[
 w_s=\binom{s+m-1}{m-1}q^s,\qquad
 Z(B,q)=\sum_{s=0}^B w_s,\qquad
 \Pr(T_B=s)=\frac{w_s}{Z(B,q)}\quad(0\le s\le B),
\]
and put \(M(B,q)=\mathbb E T_B\), \(v(B,q)=\operatorname{Var}T_B\), and \(v_y=v(B_y,q)\). The binomial coefficient counts the nonnegative transverse vectors of total \(s\), so the original conditional law of \(X_\Sigma\) given \(Y=y\) is exactly \(T_{B_y}\). In particular, \(V:=\mathbb E U^2=\sum_y p_yv_y\).

First establish the source constraints and height bounds. Strict positivity gives \(j>0\), hence \(j\ge1\). The original slack \(A=L-X_\Sigma-hY\) is nonnegative everywhere and positive at the positive-probability origin. Its mean \(B_1-mj\) is therefore a strictly positive integer, so \(B_1\ge m+1\). Since \(L\ge2h\), one has \(h\le B_1\) and \(B_0\le2B_1\).

Let \(G_1,\ldots,G_m\) be independent geometric variables with \(\Pr(G_i=s)=(1-q)q^s\) for \(s\ge0\), and put \(G=\sum_iG_i\) and \(\mu=q/(1-q)\). The exact slice-law identity is \(T_B\stackrel{\mathrm{law}}=G\mid(G\le B)\). Every finite-budget conditional mean is strictly less than \(m\mu\), since both the conditioning event and its complement have positive probability and all values on the latter exceed all values on the former. Averaging gives \(j<\mu\), and consequently \(q>1/2\) and \(\mu>1\).

The weights \(w_s\) are log-concave, since \(w_{s+1}/w_s=q(s+m)/(s+1)\) is nonincreasing. Their partial sums are also log-concave: for \(B\ge1\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 Z(B,q)^2-Z(B-1,q)Z(B+1,q)
 &=w_Bw_0+\sum_{s=0}^{B-1}
                (w_Bw_{s+1}-w_{B+1}w_s)\ge0.
\end{aligned}
\]
The ratio ordering gives each summand's sign. Taking products of successive partition ratios over adjacent intervals of length \(h\) shows that the positive height masses \(p_y\propto e^{\theta y}Z(B_y,q)\) are log-concave on \(\{0,\ldots,K\}\).

The exact height mean equation is
\[
 p_0=\sum_{y=2}^K(y-1)p_y.
\tag{1}
\]
In particular \(p_0\ge p_2\). Also \(p_0\le2p_1\): otherwise \(r=p_1/p_0<1/2\), and height log-concavity gives \(p_y\le p_0r^y\). Substitution into (1) would give
\(p_0\le p_0r^2/(1-r)^2<p_0\), a contradiction. Markov's inequality gives \(p_0+p_1=\Pr(Y<2)\ge1/2\), and hence
\[
 p_1\ge\frac16.
\tag{2}
\]

Define the adjacent partition-curvature ratio
\(R(q)=Z(B_0,q)Z(B_2,q)/Z(B_1,q)^2\). It obeys \(0<R(q)\le1\). The original probabilities satisfy \(p_0p_2/p_1^2=R(q)\), regardless of \(K\). Write \(a_{\mathrm h}=p_0/p_1\) and \(b_{\mathrm h}=p_2/p_1\). Equation (1) gives \(a_{\mathrm h}\ge b_{\mathrm h}\), so \(b_{\mathrm h}\le\sqrt{R(q)}\). If \(R(q)\le1/4\), log-concavity gives \(p_y/p_1\le b_{\mathrm h}^{y-1}\) for \(y\ge1\), and (1) implies
\(a_{\mathrm h}\le b_{\mathrm h}/(1-b_{\mathrm h})^2\le4\sqrt{R(q)}\). If \(R(q)>1/4\), the already proved \(a_{\mathrm h}\le2\) gives the same bound. Thus
\[
 \frac{p_0}{p_1}\le4\sqrt{R(q)},\qquad
 p_0\le4\sqrt{R(q)}.
\tag{3}
\]

For \(m=1\), use the all-budget scalar estimates in accepted fact `844fb74d3b46622a`. With \(s=1-q\) and \(M_1=\min\{B_1,s^{-1}\}\), that fact gives \(v_1\ge M_1^2/768\), since \(B_1\ge2\), and gives \(\mathbb E[(T_B-\mathbb ET_B)^4]\le384\min\{B^4,s^{-4}\}\) for every \(B\ge0\). These are its scalar estimates for arbitrary budgets, not its three-height source conclusion. Equations (2) and \(B_y\le B_0\le2B_1\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 V&\ge\frac{M_1^2}{4608},\\
 \mathbb E U^4&\le6144M_1^4
      \le6144\cdot4608^2V^2<2^{37}V^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
This includes every zero-budget slice. It remains to treat \(m\ge2\).

We need two elementary consequences of lattice log-concavity. If a nonnegative integer-valued variable \(D\) has positive log-concave masses on \(\{0,\ldots,b\}\), then its survival probabilities \(Q_k=\Pr(D\ge k)\) are log-concave. Indeed, on their positive support the ratios of the mass at \(k+r\) to the mass at \(k\) are nonincreasing in \(k\). Summation makes \(Q_k/\Pr(D=k)\) nonincreasing, so \(Q_{k+1}/Q_k\) is nonincreasing. Since \(Q_0=1\), this gives \(Q_{a+b}\le Q_aQ_b\) and \(Q_k\le Q_1^k\). Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Var}D&\le(\mathbb ED)(1+\mathbb ED),\\
 \mathbb ED&\le\frac{1-\Pr(D=0)}{\Pr(D=0)}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]
For the first inequality, the tail identity and the preceding product bound give
\(\mathbb E[D(D-1)]/2=\sum_{a,b\ge1}Q_{a+b}\le(\mathbb ED)^2\). The second inequality follows by summing \(Q_k\le Q_1^k\). Deterministic variables obey these bounds as well.

It follows that \(v(B,q)\) is nondecreasing in its integer budget. To check this directly, add the last atom to the law at budget \(B-1\), and let \(\alpha=w_B/Z(B,q)\). Write \(d=1+\mathbb E[B-1-T_{B-1}]\). The reversed law \(B-T_B\) is log-concave with mass \(\alpha\) at zero and mean \((1-\alpha)d\). The second bound in (4) gives \(\alpha d\le1\); the first bound applied to \(B-1-T_{B-1}\) gives \(v(B-1,q)\le d(d-1)\). The mixture variance identity now gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 v(B,q)-v(B-1,q)
 &=\alpha\bigl((1-\alpha)d^2-v(B-1,q)\bigr)\ge0.
\end{aligned}
\]
The initial variance at budget zero is zero. As \(B\to\infty\), the first two conditional moments converge to those of \(G\), so
\[
 v(B,q)\le\sigma^2:=m\mu(1+\mu),\qquad
 v_y\le v_1\quad(y\ge1).
\tag{5}
\]

Each finite conditional total law is log-concave. The general scalar estimate proved as equation (3) in accepted fact `38622219f22cea58`, including its deterministic case, therefore gives
\[
 \mathbb E U^4\le20000\left(\sum_{y=0}^Kp_yv_y^2+V\right).
\tag{6}
\]
We will bound the squared-variance average and also show \(V\ge1/96\).

Abbreviate \(B=B_1\) and \(t=B/m\ge1\), and set \(q_*=B/(B+m)\). First suppose \(q\le q_*\), equivalently \(\mu\le t\). The elementary geometric centered-moment formula and independence give
\[
 \mathbb E(G-m\mu)^4
 =3\sigma^4+m\mu(1+\mu)(1+6\mu+6\mu^2)
 \le10\sigma^4.
\tag{7}
\]
The formula follows by differentiating the geometric series four times; the bound uses \(\mu\ge1\) and \(m\ge2\). If \(W=G-m\mu\), Hölder gives \(\mathbb E|W|\ge\sigma/\sqrt{10}\), centering gives \(\mathbb EW_-=(\mathbb E|W|)/2\), and Cauchy-Schwarz gives
\(\Pr(G\le m\mu)\ge(\mathbb EW_-)^2/\sigma^2\ge1/40\). Since \(B\ge m\mu\), the middle conditioning probability is at least \(1/40\).

The unconditioned sum \(G\) has every atom at most \(2/\sigma\). For a direct check, its one-variable characteristic function has squared modulus
\([1+4\mu(1+\mu)\sin^2(u/2)]^{-1}\). Fourier coefficient inversion and \(\sin(|u|/2)\ge |u|/\pi\) on \([-\pi,\pi]\) imply
\[
 \max_s\Pr(G=s)
 \le\frac{1}{4\sqrt{\mu(1+\mu)}}
       \int_{\mathbb R}(1+x^2)^{-m/2}\,dx
 <\frac2\sigma.
\]
Indeed, the integral is less than \(7/\sqrt m\): its part on \([-1,1]\) is at most \(2\sqrt\pi/\sqrt m\), using \(\log(1+x^2)\ge x^2/2\); its remaining part is at most \(2/(m-1)\le2\sqrt2/\sqrt m\). The sum of the two numerical coefficients is less than 7. Conditioning consequently bounds every middle atom by \(80/\sigma\).

If \(\sigma\ge640\), an interval of radius \(\sigma/640\) about the conditional mean contains at most \(\sigma/320+2\) integers and has probability at most \(1/2\). Hence \(v_1\ge\sigma^2/(2\cdot640^2)\). If \(\sigma<640\), the middle support contains the unconditioned mode \(k=\lfloor(m-1)\mu\rfloor\), since \(1\le k\le m\mu\le B\). The atom immediately to its left has at least half of the mode's probability, because \(k\ge m-1\) and \(w_{k-1}/w_k=k/[q(k+m-1)]\ge1/2\). If the mode's probability is at least \(1/2\), the product of these neighboring probabilities gives \(v_1\ge1/8\). Otherwise, for the middle masses \(u_i\),
\(v_1=\frac12\sum_{i,j}u_iu_j(i-j)^2\ge(1-\max_i u_i)/2>1/4\).
Thus in this chamber
\[
 v_1\ge\frac18,\qquad
 v_1\ge2^{-22}\sigma^2,
 \qquad
 \sum_y p_yv_y^2\le\sigma^4\le2^{44}v_1^2.
\tag{8}
\]
The small-\(\sigma\) denominator \(8\cdot640^2=3276800\) is less than \(2^{22}\); equation (5) proves the final bound.

Now suppose \(q\ge q_*\). Define the auxiliary tilt parameter \(a=1-q_*/q\), so \(0\le a<1/(t+1)\le1/2\), and use the convention \(a^{-1}=+\infty\) when \(a=0\). We prove the refined middle variance bound
\[
 v_1\ge\frac1{16},\qquad
 v_1\ge2^{-28}\min\{mt^2,a^{-2}\}.
\tag{9}
\]
Let \(\ell=\min\{\sqrt m\,t,a^{-1}\}\), \(n=\lfloor\ell/256\rfloor\), and choose the middle mode
\(k=\min\{B,\lfloor(m-1)\mu\rfloor\}\). Since \(\mu\ge t\), one has \(k\ge\lfloor B/2\rfloor\ge B/3\) and \(B-k\le t+1\le2t\). Also \(n\le B/(256\sqrt m)\), so \(k-j>B/4\) for every \(0\le j\le n\).

For real \(s\ge B/4\), the logarithmic derivative of \(s/(s+m-1)\) is at most \(16/(mt^2)\). Consequently, for integer \(s\in[B/4,B]\),
\[
 \frac{w_{s-1}}{w_s}
 =\frac{s}{q(s+m-1)}
 \ge(1-a)\exp\left(-\frac{16(B-s)}{mt^2}\right).
\]
Multiplying these leftward ratios and using \(\log(1-a)\ge-2a\) gives, for \(0\le j\le n\),
\[
 \log\frac{w_{k-j}}{w_k}
 \ge-2aj-\frac{32j}{mt}-\frac{8j^2}{mt^2}
 \ge-\frac{2}{256}-\frac{32}{256\sqrt m}
                           -\frac{8}{256^2}>-\frac14.
\]
Thus each of these \(n+1>\ell/256\) atoms has at least half the mode's weight, and every middle atom has probability less than \(512/\ell\). If \(\ell\ge4096\), an interval of radius \(\ell/4096\) about the middle mean has probability at most
\((\ell/2048+2)512/\ell\le1/2\), proving \(v_1\ge\ell^2/2^{25}\).
For every \(\ell\), the atom immediately to the left of the mode has at least one quarter of its probability: \(k\ge B/3\ge(m+1)/3\) gives \(k/(k+m-1)\ge1/4\). The same neighboring-atom or maximum-atom argument used above therefore gives \(v_1\ge1/16\). For \(\ell<4096\), this implies \(v_1\ge\ell^2/(16\cdot4096^2)=\ell^2/2^{28}\). This proves (9), including \(a=0\).

We also have the budget-uniform upper bound
\[
 v_0\le288mt^2.
\tag{10}
\]
For \(m=2,3\), the bounded-support variance bound gives \(v_0\le B_0^2/4\le B^2=m^2t^2\le3mt^2\). For \(m\ge4\) and \(\mu\le4t\), equation (5) gives \(v_0\le m\mu(1+\mu)\le20mt^2\). If \(m\ge4\) and \(\mu>4t\), the consecutive weight ratios of the height-zero slack \(B_0-T_{B_0}\) are at most
\[
 \frac{B_0}{q(B_0+m-1)}
 \le\frac{2B+m/2}{2B+m-1}
 \le1-\frac{m}{12B}.
\]
Here \(B_0\le2B\), \(1/q=1+1/\mu<1+m/(4B)\), \(m/2-1\ge m/4\), and \(2B+m-1\le3B\) justify the comparisons. A shift of the slack weights gives its tail bound \(\Pr(B_0-T_{B_0}\ge u)\le r^u\), where \(r=1-m/(12B)\). Summing \((2u-1)r^u\) bounds the slack second moment by \(2/(1-r)^2=288t^2\), and proves (10).

Put \(\rho=h/B\in(0,1]\) and \(x=m\rho^2\). The refined variance comparison is
\[
 \frac{v_0}{v_1}\le2^{41}(1+x).
\tag{11}
\]
To prove it, set \(q_{0,*}=B_0/(B_0+m)\) and
\(\Delta=\rho/[t(1+\rho)+1]\), so \(q_{0,*}/q_*=1+\Delta\).
If \(a\le2\Delta\), equations (9)-(10) give
\[
 \frac{v_0}{v_1}
 \le2^{37}\max\{1,mt^2a^2\}
 \le2^{37}\max\{1,4m\rho^2\}
 \le2^{39}(1+x).
\]
If \(a>2\Delta\) but \(a\le4/(\sqrt m\,t)\), the same bound is at most \(2^{41}\). In the remaining case, put \(a_0=1-q_{0,*}/q=a-(1-a)\Delta>a/2\). Since \(a>4/(\sqrt m\,t)\), one has \(1/(B_0+m-1)\le1/B<a/4\). Therefore the height-zero slack ratios are at most
\[
 \frac{B_0}{q(B_0+m-1)}
 =(1-a_0)\left(1+\frac1{B_0+m-1}\right)
 \le(1-a/2)(1+a/4)\le1-a/4.
\]
The preceding shift-and-tail argument gives \(v_0\le32/a^2\). Equation (9), with \(a>4/(\sqrt m\,t)\), gives \(v_1\ge2^{-28}/a^2\), so the ratio is at most \(2^{33}\). These three cases prove (11).

It remains to bound the actual source mass multiplying the large variance. Accepted fact `5fa48a554f30f367`, equations (2)-(5) in its proof, establishes that for every fixed \(m\ge2\) and \(q\in(0,1)\), the integer-budget function \(B\mapsto M(B,q)\) is concave. Its \(M(B,q),Z(B,q),w_s\) are precisely the objects defined here. That budget-concavity proof uses no height probabilities and no restriction on \(h/B_1\). It therefore gives
\[
 \frac{d}{d\log q}\log R(q)
 =M(B+h,q)+M(B-h,q)-2M(B,q)\le0.
\tag{12}
\]
This is the universal partition assertion from that accepted proof, not an application of its three-height probability formula.

At \(q=q_*\), the auxiliary geometric mean is \(\mu=t\), so the unconditioned sum has mean \(B\). Write \(F_i=\Pr(G\le B_i)\) at this value. Equation (7) and its one-sided argument give \(F_1\ge1/40\), and \(F_0\le1\). We claim \(F_2\le e^{-m\rho^2/4}\). For \(\lambda=\rho/(1+\mu)\), the exact geometric Laplace transform is
\(\mathbb Ee^{-\lambda G_i}=[1+\mu(1-e^{-\lambda})]^{-1}\).
Using \(1-e^{-\lambda}\ge\lambda-\lambda^2/2\), \(1-e^{-\lambda}\le\lambda\), and \(\log(1+u)\ge u-u^2/2\) for \(u\ge0\), we obtain
\(\log\mathbb Ee^{-\lambda G_i}\le-\mu\lambda+\mu(1+\mu)\lambda^2/2\).
Markov's inequality at \(B_2=(1-\rho)m\mu\) consequently gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \log F_2
 &\le m\left(-\rho\mu\lambda
                    +\frac{\mu(1+\mu)\lambda^2}{2}\right)\\
 &=-\frac{m\rho^2\mu}{2(1+\mu)}\le-\frac{m\rho^2}{4}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The argument remains valid when \(B_2=0\). Since \(Z(B_i,q_*)=(1-q_*)^{-m}F_i\), it follows that \(R(q_*)\le1600e^{-x/4}\). Equations (3) and (12) thus prove the original-source suppression
\[
 p_0\le160e^{-x/8}\qquad(q\ge q_*).
\tag{13}
\]

Combining (11) and (13) gives
\[
 p_0v_0^2
 \le160\cdot2^{82}(1+x)^2e^{-x/8}v_1^2
 \le2^{98}v_1^2.
\tag{14}
\]
Indeed, for \(x\ge0\), the function \((1+x)^2e^{-x/8}\) is maximized at \(x=15\) and is at most \(256=2^8\), while \(160<2^8\). By (5), all heights \(y\ge1\) have \(v_y\le v_1\), so in the high-\(q\) chamber \(\sum_y p_yv_y^2\le2^{99}v_1^2\). Equation (8) gives this same coarse bound in the low-\(q\) chamber. The bounds \(v_1\ge1/16\) and \(p_1\ge1/6\) in both chambers imply
\[
 V\ge\frac1{96},\qquad
 \sum_y p_yv_y^2\le2^{99}v_1^2
             \le36\cdot2^{99}V^2<2^{105}V^2.
\]
Finally, (6) gives
\(\mathbb E U^4\le20000(2^{105}+96)V^2<2^{121}V^2\), since \(20000<2^{15}\) and \(2^{105}+96<2^{106}\). Together with the rank-one case, this proves the theorem for every original source in the statement. All height weights used throughout are the original partition-determined weights; no conditional mean was assumed integral.
statement:
Let \(m,h,L\) be positive integers with \(K:=\lfloor L/h\rfloor\ge2\), and let \(\beta<0\) and \(\theta\in\mathbb R\) be finite. Let \((\mathbf X,Y)\) have the strictly positive original law
\[
 p(\mathbf x,y)=\frac{\exp(\beta\sum_{i=1}^m x_i+\theta y)}{\mathcal Z},
 \qquad
 E_{L,h,m}=\left\{(\mathbf x,y)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^{m+1}:
                         \sum_{i=1}^m x_i+hy\le L\right\}.
\]
Suppose its full mean is \((j\mathbf1,1)\), where \(j\) is an integer. Define the transverse total \(X_\Sigma:=\sum_{i=1}^mX_i\) and its original height-conditioned noise \(U:=X_\Sigma-\mathbb E[X_\Sigma\mid Y]\). Then
\[
 \mathbb E U^4\le2^{121}(\mathbb E U^2)^2.
\]
The constant is independent of \(m,h,L,\beta,\theta,j,K\). The objects \(X_\Sigma,q=e^\beta,B_y=L-hy,Z(B,q),M(B,q)\), and \(v_y\) below have exactly the transverse-total, tilt, budget, partition, conditional-total-mean, and conditional-total-variance meanings used in accepted fact `5fa48a554f30f367`. For \(m=1\), the truncated scalar law is exactly that in accepted fact `844fb74d3b46622a`, with its centered scalar noise \(N\) equal to \(U\). The general finite lattice log-concave fourth-moment estimate used below is the one proved as equation (3) of accepted fact `38622219f22cea58`; its scalar variable \(V\) is replaced by one conditional transverse total, rather than by that fact's radial lattice law.
